quest.title: The Exile: Blooming
quest.description: A rose that once bloomed in Sumeru City may be able to bloom elsewhere, too.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Delicious Butter Chicken x1, Sumeru Rose x1

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: If it weren't for you, I don't think I'd have ever seen these roses sprout.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: If only I knew this would happen... instead of seeds, I should have brought a few more books.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Are you surprised? Well, I guess that means that I've adapted pretty well.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: When I first got here, I was unable to get used to anything, whether it be the food, the housing, or anything else.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: But I got used to everything over time.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: That doesn't mean that I've fully accepted my predicament, though.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I suppose it is impossible to make roses from Sumeru City bloom here after all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you a researcher?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I could have been called that once, but not anymore.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I said something beyond my station, and learned something I shouldn't have.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I broke the Akademiya's taboos, so I was removed from amongst their ranks.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What did you say?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Curiosity is the impetus for seeking wisdom, but it's also the cause of sin.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I only understood that after I was exiled to this place.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: For safety reasons, I don't think I should go into details.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: All right then.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Ahem, but...

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I thought adventurers would just come and go, never coming back to chit-chat after finishing their jobs.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I didn't expect to have another long conversation with you.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: To be honest, I don't have a lot of friends to talk to here.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Do you think... at some point... you would be able to come by and fertilize my plants again?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: ...Okay then, I'll wait for you.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: You probably don't know much about them... but they are very versatile, and have many uses.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: They can be eaten, turned into medicine, given as gifts, or fetch a good price on the market.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: And that's just some of the more common applications.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: The flower, leaves, and stalk of a Sumeru Rose also did not always look like this. They all had different appearances once upon a time.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I believe geographical changes led to changes in the roses' traits.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: A study of its traits could help us derive past geographical and historical information.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I won't be able to explain the mechanism over just a casual conversation, and sharing such information with adventurers is probably against the rules as well.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: If you're interested in botanical evolution, you should visit the Akademiya. They'll have more on the subject.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you're doing this for your research?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I'm not a researcher anymore. I no longer have the right or means to pursue any research.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: If you must know why... *sigh*, you are a very curious soul, you know that?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I grew a lot of Sumeru Roses back in my former residence. The flowers were spectacular, and I got to see them every day.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: If it was possible, I wish I could see them again, just like before.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: ...That's all there is to it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can understand that.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: There you are. You're very punctual.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I made some Butter Chicken. You're welcome to dine with me if you're hungry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Butter Chicken! How could we refuse? A big plate for Paimon, please!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, sorry...

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: It's okay, there's no need to be so formal. It's only human nature to love food.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I'll heat some up and pack it for you. It's the least I could do to show my gratitude for your help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're so nice, Miss Sabbah! Your roses will surely grow and flower, just like you wanted!

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Well, I've been keeping the soil moist, so the sprouts have been coming along.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: My only worry is that they are growing slowly.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Generally speaking, if a germ is in good shape, it should grow quickly enough, but these few have been dormant so far...

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I'm not sure if it's because the soil isn't fertile enough. I may have to add more fertilizer if this keeps up.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Would you do me this favor, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Piece of cake. We got this!

choices.text: We can try using Dendro again.

talks.objective: Use the power of Dendro to "fertilize" the sprouts

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Thank you again. Honestly, it gladdens my heart to see Sumeru Roses grow in this environment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you talk to Sabbah, new leaves begin to sprout...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The leaves unfold, revealing flower buds.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The flower buds slowly open and blossom into Sumeru Roses.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sabbah picks one and hands it to you and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You shouldn't have... You didn't have many to begin with...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: It's all right. After all, this wouldn't have been possible without your help.

choices.text: We were just lending a hand.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: A rose garden is magnificent, but a single rose also has beauty of its own. I've been intrigued by roses ever since my scholarly days.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? You were a researcher?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Right, I haven't told you yet... I'm not a native of Aaru Village. I "moved" here from the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See, didn't Paimon tell you that Miss Sabbah speaks in a refined way, just like the researchers we've met?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You planted these because you wanted to continue studying roses, right?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I wouldn't say that. To be honest, I don't think that researchers' interest in their subjects should be cultivated just for research's sake alone.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I did this because I love this world and want to understand the life cycle of plants.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: As for me, I once studied the impact of geographical changes on the evolution of roses.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Just consider this. If the environments in Sumeru had changed in a totally different way, how would these roses have adapted?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Would they have crawled up the walls like ivy? If so, the walls of the Akademiya would now be covered in roses.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Would they have formed clusters? A natural bouquet! Wouldn't that have been lovely?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Maybe they might have even developed a spectrum of colors... White, red, and gold... Brand new species in their own right.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Of course, very few people discover new species nowadays, much less develop new species like the top researchers used to do.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: What I want to say is that there's a vast amount of potential in every rose.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Exploring the possibilities is a lot of fun for me. Back then, I would happily collect samples every day.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Looking back now, that was a simple and joyful time.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Anyway, just take it. To me, this is no loss. I am freely sharing my happiness.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: If you still feel awkward, just visit me often, and bring some Sumeru Roses with you.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I feel at ease when I talk to you.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: And no matter what I said, you never thought it was nonsense or interrupted me.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I'll have small gifts for you too. Though I have no use for them now, you might like them.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll be back.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Please do return.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Here for a chat? I've been wanting to talk to somebody.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: You don't seem to have a Vision, and yet you can control Dendro. You're no ordinary adventurer, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Supposedly, there are people who can control the elements without a Vision, but such people are of universally ill repute...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: You, however, have a good heart. Don't stray onto the wrong path!
